t: Find Sorted Submatrices With Maximum Element at Most K
o: Count submatrices where every element ≤ k and every row is non-increasing across the chosen columns. Rows are independent: for each cell (r, j) define run[r][j] = length of the longest non-increasing, all-≤k segment of row r ending at column j. A submatrix with bottom row b, right column d, top row a, and width w is valid iff w ≤ min(run[a..b][d]). So for each column d we need, for every bottom row, the sum over top rows of that range minimum — the classic 'sum of subarray minimums' streaming computation with a monotonic stack, done once per column.
k: Reduce rows to run lengths: validity of a submatrix anchored at (bottom b, right column d) with width w depends only on min of run[a..b][d] being ≥ w.
For a fixed column, Σ_a min(run[a..b]) over all bottoms b is computable online with a monotonic stack in O(m) per column.
Total complexity O(mn), essential since m, n ≤ 1000 rules out quadratic-in-area enumeration.

a.n: Approach 1: Row-pair expansion with running minimum
a.i: Fix a top row; extend the bottom row downward while maintaining per-column minimum run length; each step adds Σ_j minRun[j] valid submatrices (one per right-column/width choice collapses into the run count). Simple and clearly correct, but O(m²n).
s: For each top row, copy run into mn; for each bottom row update mn[j] = min(mn[j], run[bot][j]) and add Σ mn to the answer
a.t: O(m²n) — clear but may be slow at the 10^3 scale (≈10^9 ops worst case)

a.i: For each column d, sweep rows top to bottom maintaining cur = Σ_{a ≤ i} min(run[a..i][d]) with a monotonic stack of (value, count) blocks. A new value v absorbs all blocks with value ≥ v (their minimum becomes v), so cur updates in amortized O(1); add cur to the answer at each row.
s: For each column, sweep rows with a monotonic stack: pop blocks with value ≥ v, merge counts, cur += v·mergedCount
Add cur to the answer after each row
a.t: O(mn) — each cell enters and leaves the monotonic stack once per column pass
a.sp: O(mn) for run lengths, O(m) per-column stack

w: Verify on example 1: column 3 has runs [3,1] contributing 3 + 2 = 5, column 2 contributes 2, columns 0–1 contribute 1 each → 8. Pitfalls: run must reset to 0 when grid[i][j] > k, and the non-increasing check compares grid[i][j-1] ≥ grid[i][j]. The answer can reach ~10^9·10^3, so use 64-bit accumulators. Follow-up: count submatrices with rows sorted non-decreasing instead — flip the comparison.
